CHAPTER 20 — सत्याग्रहाश्रमः (SATYAGRAHASHRAMAH)

Introduction — पाठपरिचयः

This lesson is a piece of simple modern Sanskrit prose (गद्यम्) describing Mahatma Gandhi's famous सत्याग्रहाश्रमः — the Satyagraha Ashram on the bank of the Sabarmati river at Ahmedabad. The word सत्याग्रहः is formed from सत्य (truth) + आग्रहः (firm insistence): 'firm insistence on truth'. The ashram was the living laboratory where Gandhiji and his companions practised truth (सत्यम्), non-violence (अहिंसा), self-reliance (स्वावलम्बनम्) and simple living. Through this lesson we learn to read simple Sanskrit prose about a real historical place, we absorb the Gandhian values it embodies, and we draw grammar (सन्धिः, विभक्तिः, शब्दरूपम्, धातुरूपम्) from the sentences we read.

1) आश्रमस्य परिचयः — Introduction to the Ashram

संस्कृतगद्यम्: भारतस्य पश्चिमभागे गुर्जरराज्ये अहमदाबादनाम प्रसिद्धं नगरम् अस्ति। तस्य नगरस्य समीपे साबरमतीनद्याः तीरे एकः पवित्रः आश्रमः विद्यते। अस्य आश्रमस्य नाम सत्याग्रहाश्रमः इति। जनाः एनं 'साबरमती-आश्रमः' इति अपि वदन्ति। महात्मा गान्धी दक्षिण-आफ्रिकादेशात् भारतं प्रत्यागत्य ख्रिस्ताब्दे १९१५ तमे वर्षे अहमदाबादनगरस्य समीपे कोचरबग्रामे एनम् आश्रमं स्थापितवान्। ततः १९१७ तमे वर्षे आश्रमः साबरमतीनद्याः तीरं नीतः। अत्र गान्धिमहोदयस्य लघु कुटीरं 'हृदयकुञ्जः' इति नाम्ना प्रसिद्धम् अस्ति।
शब्दार्थ: पश्चिमभागे = in the western part; गुर्जरराज्ये = in the state of Gujarat; समीपे = near; नद्याः तीरे = on the bank of the river; पवित्रः = holy, pure; विद्यते = exists, is; प्रत्यागत्य = having returned; ख्रिस्ताब्दे = in the year (CE); स्थापितवान् = established; नीतः = was taken/shifted; कुटीरम् = cottage, hut; नाम्ना = by the name.
Translation: In the western part of India, in the state of Gujarat, there is a famous city named Ahmedabad. Near that city, on the bank of the river Sabarmati, there is a holy ashram. Its name is the Satyagraha Ashram; people also call it the Sabarmati Ashram. Mahatma Gandhi, having returned to India from South Africa, established this ashram in the year 1915 CE at the village Kochrab near Ahmedabad. Then, in 1917, the ashram was shifted to the bank of the Sabarmati. Here Gandhiji's small cottage is famous by the name 'Hriday Kunj' (the bower of the heart).

2) आश्रमजीवनम् — Daily Life in the Ashram

संस्कृतगद्यम्: आश्रमे जीवनं सरलं नियमबद्धं च आसीत्। आश्रमवासिनः ब्राह्ममुहूर्ते एव उत्तिष्ठन्ति स्म। प्रातःकाले सायङ्काले च सर्वे मिलित्वा प्रार्थनां कुर्वन्ति स्म। प्रार्थनायाः अनन्तरं सर्वे स्वं स्वं कार्यं कुर्वन्ति स्म। केचन क्षेत्रे कृषिकार्यं कुर्वन्ति स्म, केचन चरखायन्त्रेण सूत्रं कर्तयन्ति स्म, केचन गोसेवां कुर्वन्ति स्म। सर्वे स्वानि वस्त्राणि स्वयं क्षालयन्ति स्म, स्वानि पात्राणि स्वयं मार्जयन्ति स्म। आश्रमे कोऽपि सेवकः नासीत्। सर्वं कार्यं सर्वे स्वयम् एव कुर्वन्ति स्म। भोजनं सात्त्विकं सरलं च आसीत्। सर्वे खादीवस्त्राणि धारयन्ति स्म। आश्रमे स्वच्छता अनुशासनं च सर्वत्र दृश्यते स्म।
शब्दार्थ: नियमबद्धम् = bound by rules, disciplined; आश्रमवासिनः = the residents of the ashram; ब्राह्ममुहूर्ते = in the early hour before sunrise; उत्तिष्ठन्ति स्म = used to get up; मिलित्वा = having gathered together; प्रार्थनाम् = prayer; अनन्तरम् = after; केचन = some (people); कृषिकार्यम् = farming work; चरखायन्त्रेण = with the spinning wheel (charkha); सूत्रं कर्तयन्ति स्म = used to spin thread; गोसेवाम् = service of cows; क्षालयन्ति स्म = used to wash; पात्राणि = utensils; मार्जयन्ति स्म = used to clean; सेवकः = servant; सात्त्विकम् = pure, wholesome; धारयन्ति स्म = used to wear; स्वच्छता = cleanliness; अनुशासनम् = discipline.
Translation: Life in the ashram was simple and disciplined. The residents rose in the early hours before dawn. In the morning and in the evening all gathered together and prayed. After the prayer everyone did his or her own allotted work. Some did farming in the fields, some spun thread on the charkha, some served the cows. All washed their own clothes and cleaned their own utensils. There was no servant in the ashram; everyone did all the work themselves. The food was pure (sattvik) and simple. All wore khadi clothes. Cleanliness and discipline were seen everywhere in the ashram.

3) आश्रमव्रतानि — The Vows of the Ashram

संस्कृतगद्यम्: आश्रमवासिनः एकादश व्रतानि पालयन्ति स्म। तानि व्रतानि — सत्यम्, अहिंसा, ब्रह्मचर्यम्, अस्तेयम्, अपरिग्रहः, शरीरश्रमः, अस्वादः, अभयम्, सर्वधर्मसमभावः, स्वदेशी, अस्पृश्यतानिवारणं च इति। एतैः व्रतैः आश्रमवासिनां जीवनं शुद्धं बलवत् च अभवत्।
Meanings of the eleven observances (एकादश व्रतानि): सत्यम् — truth in thought, word and deed; अहिंसा — non-violence, harming no creature; ब्रह्मचर्यम् — self-control, purity of conduct; अस्तेयम् — non-stealing, not taking what is not one's own; अपरिग्रहः — non-possession, not hoarding more than one needs; शरीरश्रमः — bread-labour, earning one's bread by one's own physical work; अस्वादः — control of the palate, eating simple food without greed for taste; अभयम् — fearlessness; सर्वधर्मसमभावः — equal respect for all religions; स्वदेशी — use of home-made, local goods; अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम् — removal of untouchability, treating every human being as equal.
Translation: The residents of the ashram observed eleven vows — truth, non-violence, celibacy/self-control, non-stealing, non-possession, bread-labour, control of the palate, fearlessness, equal regard for all religions, swadeshi, and the removal of untouchability. By these vows the life of the ashram-dwellers became pure and strong.

4) सत्यम् अहिंसा च — Truth and Non-violence (with supporting verses)

गान्धिमहोदयस्य जीवनस्य द्वे महाव्रते आस्ताम् — सत्यम् अहिंसा च। सः वदति स्म — सत्यम् एव ईश्वरः इति। For Gandhiji truth and non-violence were inseparable — two sides of the same coin: truth is the goal, non-violence is the path.
(क) मुण्डकोपनिषदः मन्त्रः (public domain): "सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः।"
शब्दार्थ: सत्यम् एव = truth alone; जयते = triumphs, wins; न अनृतम् = not falsehood; सत्येन = by truth; पन्थाः = the path; विततः = is spread, laid out; देवयानः = leading to the gods (the divine path).
Translation: Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood; by truth is laid out the divine path. This mantra from the Mundaka Upanishad — सत्यमेव जयते — is the national motto of India, inscribed below the national emblem.
(ख) "अहिंसा परमो धर्मः" — this ancient maxim, famous from the Mahabharata, means: non-violence is the highest dharma (duty/virtue). अहिंसा is the giving up of injury to any living being — मनसा वाचा कर्मणा — in mind, in speech and in action.
(ग) योगसूत्रम् (२.३५): "अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायां तत्सन्निधौ वैरत्यागः।"
शब्दार्थ: अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायाम् = when non-violence is firmly established; तत्सन्निधौ = in his presence; वैरत्यागः = abandonment of hostility.
Translation: When a person is firmly established in non-violence, beings give up hostility in his presence. This was seen in Gandhiji's own life — his ahimsa disarmed even his opponents.

5) स्वावलम्बनं सरलजीवनं च — Self-reliance and Simple Living

संस्कृतगद्यम्: आश्रमस्य महत् शिक्षणं स्वावलम्बनम् अस्ति। स्वस्य कार्यं स्वयम् एव करणं स्वावलम्बनम् इति कथ्यते। आश्रमवासिनः स्वहस्तेन एव सूत्रं कर्तयित्वा खादीवस्त्राणि निर्मान्ति स्म। ते स्वदेशीवस्तूनाम् एव उपयोगं कुर्वन्ति स्म। तेषां जीवनं सरलम् आसीत्, चिन्तनम् उच्चम् आसीत्। श्रमः एव तेषां पूजा आसीत्।
शब्दार्थ: शिक्षणम् = teaching, lesson; स्वावलम्बनम् = self-reliance; करणम् = doing; स्वहस्तेन = with one's own hand; कर्तयित्वा = having spun; निर्मान्ति स्म = used to make; स्वदेशीवस्तूनाम् = of home-made things; उपयोगम् = use; सरलम् = simple; चिन्तनम् = thinking; उच्चम् = high; श्रमः = labour.
Translation: The great teaching of the ashram is self-reliance. Doing one's own work oneself is called svavalambana. The residents spun thread with their own hands and made khadi cloth. They used only swadeshi (home-made) goods. Their living was simple, their thinking was high. Labour itself was their worship. From this very ashram, on 12 March 1930, Gandhiji set out with his companions on the famous Dandi March (the Salt Satyagraha), vowing not to return to the ashram until India won freedom. Today the Sabarmati Ashram stands as a national memorial and museum, where visitors from all over the world come to see Hriday Kunj, the charkha and Gandhiji's simple way of life.

6) व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Lesson

(A) सन्धिः (joining of sounds) and सन्धि-विच्छेदः (splitting):
  • सत्य + आग्रहः = सत्याग्रहः (अ + आ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः).
  • न + अनृतम् = नानृतम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः) — from the mantra सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम्.
  • सत्यम् + एव = सत्यमेव (the final म् joins the following vowel).
  • परमः + धर्मः = परमो धर्मः (विसर्गसन्धिः — visarga ः becomes ओ before a soft consonant).
  • कः + अपि = कोऽपि ('anyone/any at all', विसर्गसन्धिः with अवग्रह).
(B) विभक्तिः (case endings) with examples from the text:
  • प्रथमा (subject): आश्रमः, गान्धी, जीवनम् — आश्रमः पवित्रः अस्ति।
  • द्वितीया (object): प्रार्थनाम्, सूत्रम्, कार्यम् — ते प्रार्थनां कुर्वन्ति स्म।
  • तृतीया (by/with): चरखायन्त्रेण, स्वहस्तेन — चरखायन्त्रेण सूत्रं कर्तयन्ति स्म।
  • पञ्चमी (from): दक्षिण-आफ्रिकादेशात् — गान्धी आफ्रिकादेशात् प्रत्यागतः।
  • षष्ठी (of): नद्याः, आश्रमस्य, गान्धिमहोदयस्य — साबरमतीनद्याः तीरे।
  • सप्तमी (in/at): आश्रमे, नगरे, तीरे, ब्राह्ममुहूर्ते — आश्रमे जीवनं सरलम् आसीत्।
(C) शब्दरूपम् — the a-stem masculine आश्रम in प्रथमा: एकवचनम् आश्रमः, द्विवचनम् आश्रमौ, बहुवचनम् आश्रमाः। Likewise ग्रामः / ग्रामौ / ग्रामाः।
(D) धातुरूपम् — verb forms seen in the lesson: वस् (to dwell) लट्लकारः: वसति (he dwells), वसन्ति (they dwell); कृ (to do): करोति (he does), कुर्वन्ति (they do); अस् (to be): अस्ति (is), सन्ति (are); past habit is shown by लट् + स्म: कुर्वन्ति स्म = 'they used to do'; and लङ्लकारः: आसीत् = 'was'.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you read simple Sanskrit prose about the सत्याग्रहाश्रमः — founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1915 at Kochrab near Ahmedabad and shifted in 1917 to the bank of the Sabarmati, with his cottage Hriday Kunj at its heart. You saw the disciplined daily life of the ashram — early rising, prayer twice a day, spinning on the charkha, farming, cow-care and doing one's own work without servants — and the eleven vows headed by सत्यम् and अहिंसा. You studied the mantra सत्यमेव जयते (Mundaka Upanishad — India's national motto), the maxim अहिंसा परमो धर्मः, and the Yoga-sutra on ahimsa. You learned the value of स्वावलम्बनम् (self-reliance) and simple living — simple life, high thinking. Finally you drew grammar from the text: दीर्घ and विसर्ग sandhi (सत्याग्रहः, नानृतम्, परमो धर्मः), the seven common vibhakti roles, the शब्दरूप of आश्रम, and verb forms like कुर्वन्ति स्म and आसीत्.

chapter_summary.title: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः (Satyagrahashramah) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 20. It describes Mahatma Gandhi's Satyagraha (Sabarmati) Ashram in simple Sanskrit prose — its history, disciplined daily life and eleven vows — explains the values of सत्य, अहिंसा and स्वावलम्बन with public-domain verses, and draws sandhi, vibhakti and verb-form grammar from the text.

sections.heading: The ashram and its history
bullets: The सत्याग्रहाश्रमः stands on the bank of the Sabarmati river near Ahmedabad in Gujarat; it is also called the Sabarmati Ashram.
Mahatma Gandhi founded it in 1915 at the village Kochrab after returning to India from South Africa; in 1917 it was shifted to the Sabarmati bank.
सत्याग्रह = सत्य + आग्रह, 'firm insistence on truth' — the ashram was the training ground for satyagraha.
Gandhiji's simple cottage there is famous as हृदयकुञ्जः (Hriday Kunj); today the ashram is a national memorial and museum.

sections.heading: Daily life and discipline
bullets: Life was simple and rule-bound (सरलं नियमबद्धं च): residents rose in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त and prayed together morning and evening.
After prayer each did allotted work — farming (कृषिकार्यम्), spinning thread on the charkha (सूत्रकर्तनम्), and cow-service (गोसेवा).
There was no servant: all washed their own clothes and cleaned their own utensils — dignity of labour in practice.
Food was sattvik and simple; all wore khadi; cleanliness (स्वच्छता) and discipline (अनुशासनम्) were seen everywhere.

sections.heading: The eleven vows
bullets: Residents observed एकादश व्रतानि — eleven vows headed by सत्यम् (truth) and अहिंसा (non-violence).
अस्तेयम् = non-stealing; अपरिग्रहः = non-possession; शरीरश्रमः = bread-labour; अस्वादः = control of the palate.
अभयम् = fearlessness; सर्वधर्मसमभावः = equal respect for all religions; स्वदेशी = use of home-made goods; अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम् = removal of untouchability.
By these vows the residents' life became pure and strong — values lived daily, not merely preached.

sections.heading: Truth and non-violence
bullets: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम् (Mundaka Upanishad): truth alone triumphs, not falsehood — this mantra is India's national motto.
अहिंसा परमो धर्मः: non-violence is the highest dharma — giving up injury in mind, speech and action (मनसा वाचा कर्मणा).
Yoga-sutra 2.35: अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायां तत्सन्निधौ वैरत्यागः — hostility ceases in the presence of one established in ahimsa.
For Gandhiji truth and non-violence were inseparable: truth the goal, non-violence the path — the basis of satyagraha's soul-force.

sections.heading: Self-reliance, simple living and grammar
bullets: स्वावलम्बनम् = doing one's own work oneself; residents spun their own thread and made khadi, using only swadeshi goods.
Their motto in practice: simple living, high thinking (सरलं जीवनम् उच्चं चिन्तनम्); labour itself was worship.
From this ashram Gandhiji began the Dandi Salt March on 12 March 1930, vowing not to return until India was free.

Grammar from the text: सत्य + आग्रहः = सत्याग्रहः and न + अनृतम् = नानृतम् (दीर्घसन्धि); परमः + धर्मः = परमो धर्मः (विसर्गसन्धि); विभक्ति roles (आश्रमे सप्तमी, चरखायन्त्रेण तृतीया); कुर्वन्ति स्म = 'used to do', आसीत् = 'was'.

key_takeaways: The Satyagraha (Sabarmati) Ashram was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1915 near Ahmedabad and shifted to the Sabarmati bank in 1917.
सत्याग्रह means 'firm insistence on truth' — सत्य + आग्रह; the ashram was its living laboratory.
Ashram life was simple and disciplined: early rising, prayer twice daily, spinning, farming, and doing one's own work without servants.
The residents kept eleven vows headed by सत्य and अहिंसा, including अस्तेय, अपरिग्रह, शरीरश्रम, अभय, सर्वधर्मसमभाव and स्वदेशी.
सत्यमेव जयते (Mundaka Upanishad) — truth alone triumphs — is India's national motto; अहिंसा परमो धर्मः declares non-violence the highest dharma.
स्वावलम्बनम् (self-reliance) and simple living — khadi, swadeshi, dignity of labour — are the ashram's lasting lessons for students today.
From the text we learn दीर्घ and विसर्ग sandhi (सत्याग्रहः, नानृतम्, परमो धर्मः), vibhakti roles, and verb forms like कुर्वन्ति स्म and आसीत्.

glossary.definition: सत्य + आग्रह — 'firm insistence on truth'; Gandhiji's method of resisting injustice by truth-force and non-violence.
A hermitage or community of disciplined, simple living devoted to shared ideals and self-work.
Truth — in thought, word and deed; the first ashram vow and, for Gandhiji, God himself.
Non-violence — giving up injury to any living being in mind, speech and action (मनसा वाचा कर्मणा).
Self-reliance — doing one's own work oneself, as the ashram residents did in spinning, washing and cleaning.
Non-stealing — not taking, or even desiring, what belongs to another.
Non-possession — not hoarding more than one genuinely needs.
Bread-labour — earning one's bread by one's own physical work; labour as worship.
Fearlessness — freedom from fear, an essential vow of the ashram discipline.
Equal respect for all religions — regarding every faith with the same goodwill.
The vow of using home-made, local goods and serving one's immediate neighbourhood.
Hand-spun, hand-woven cloth — the fabric of self-reliance made on the charkha.
Prayer — held collectively in the ashram every morning and evening.
'Bower of the heart' — the name of Gandhiji's simple cottage at the Sabarmati Ashram.
Splitting a joined sandhi form back into its parts, e.g. सत्याग्रहः = सत्य + आग्रहः.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — सत्याग्रहाश्रमः (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 20)

questions.question: महात्मा गान्धी सत्याग्रहाश्रमं कस्मिन् ख्रिस्ताब्दे स्थापितवान्? (In which year did Mahatma Gandhi found the Satyagraha Ashram?)
questions.explanation: Gandhiji founded the ashram in 1915 at Kochrab near Ahmedabad, after returning from South Africa.

questions.question: 'सत्यमेव जयते' इति मन्त्रः कुतः गृहीतः? (From where is the mantra 'Satyameva Jayate' taken?)
questions.answer: मुण्डकोपनिषदः
questions.explanation: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम् is from the Mundaka Upanishad; it is India's national motto.

questions.question: रिक्तस्थानं पूरयत — अहिंसा परमो ______। (Fill in the blank.)
questions.answer: धर्मः
questions.explanation: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः — non-violence is the highest dharma.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः साबरमतीनद्याः तीरे अस्ति। (The Satyagraha Ashram is on the bank of the Sabarmati river.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The ashram stands on the bank of the Sabarmati near Ahmedabad, hence its other name Sabarmati Ashram.

questions.question: 'सत्याग्रह' इति शब्दस्य कः अर्थः? पदद्वयं विभज्य लिखत। (What does the word सत्याग्रह mean? Split it into its two parts.)
questions.answer: सत्याग्रह = सत्य (truth) + आग्रह (firm insistence) — 'firm insistence on truth'. It is Gandhiji's method of resisting injustice through truth-force and non-violence, not physical force.
questions.explanation: The join is दीर्घसन्धि: अ + आ = आ.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत — (a) सत्याग्रहः (b) नानृतम्। (Split the sandhi.)
questions.answer: (a) सत्याग्रहः = सत्य + आग्रहः (अ + आ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः). (b) नानृतम् = न + अनृतम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः).
questions.explanation: Both are examples of दीर्घसन्धि, where similar vowels merge into one long vowel.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनां दिनचर्यां संक्षेपेण वर्णयत। (Describe briefly the daily routine of the ashram residents.)
questions.answer: The residents rose in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त (before dawn) and gathered for prayer in the morning and evening. After prayer each did allotted work — farming, spinning thread on the charkha, cow-service. All washed their own clothes and cleaned their own utensils; there was no servant. Food was sattvik and simple, and all wore khadi. Cleanliness and discipline marked the whole day.
questions.explanation: Key points: early rising, twice-daily prayer, allotted work (spinning/farming/cow-care), self-help, simple food, khadi.

questions.question: आश्रमव्रतेषु कानिचन षड् व्रतानि नामनिर्देशपूर्वकं सार्थं लिखत। (Name any six of the ashram vows with their meanings.)
questions.answer: Any six, e.g.: सत्यम् — truth in thought, word and deed; अहिंसा — non-violence, harming no creature; अस्तेयम् — non-stealing; अपरिग्रहः — non-possession, not hoarding beyond need; शरीरश्रमः — bread-labour, earning by one's own physical work; अभयम् — fearlessness. (Also acceptable: ब्रह्मचर्यम्, अस्वादः, सर्वधर्मसमभावः, स्वदेशी, अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम्.)
questions.explanation: The residents observed eleven vows (एकादश व्रतानि); any six with correct meanings earn full marks.

questions.question: सत्यम् अहिंसा च — explain these two great vows of Gandhiji's life, quoting the mantra सत्यमेव जयते and the maxim अहिंसा परमो धर्मः with their meanings. How are truth and non-violence related in satyagraha?
questions.answer: सत्यम् (truth) means truthfulness in thought, word and deed; Gandhiji even said 'Truth is God'. The Mundaka Upanishad declares: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम् — 'Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood; by truth is laid the divine path.' This mantra is India's national motto. अहिंसा (non-violence) is the giving up of injury to any living being — मनसा वाचा कर्मणा, in mind, speech and action. The ancient maxim says: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः — non-violence is the highest dharma. In satyagraha the two are inseparable: truth is the goal and non-violence is the path. A satyagrahi resists injustice firmly but without hatred or violence, relying on soul-force rather than physical force; as the Yoga-sutra says, in the presence of one established in ahimsa even hostility ceases (अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायां तत्सन्निधौ वैरत्यागः).
questions.explanation: Full answer quotes both sayings, gives their meanings, and explains truth as the goal and non-violence as the path of satyagraha.

questions.question: स्वावलम्बनम् — what is self-reliance as taught by the Satyagraha Ashram? Describe how the residents practised it, and write how a student can practise स्वावलम्बन and simple living today.
questions.answer: स्वावलम्बनम् means self-reliance — doing one's own work oneself (स्वस्य कार्यं स्वयम् एव करणम्). In the ashram there were no servants: residents rose early, washed their own clothes, cleaned their own utensils, grew food, served the cows, and spun thread on the charkha to make their own khadi cloth, using only swadeshi goods. Labour itself was their worship, and their life showed 'simple living, high thinking' (सरलं जीवनम् उच्चं चिन्तनम्). A student today can practise the same values by: keeping his or her own room, books and clothes clean and in order; doing homework and chores without depending on others; avoiding waste and needless possessions (अपरिग्रह); preferring simple food and simple dress; respecting all kinds of labour; and using local, hand-made products where possible. Such habits build self-confidence, dignity of labour and strength of character.
questions.explanation: Definition, ashram practices (no servants, spinning, khadi, swadeshi), and at least three concrete applications for a student.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः कस्मिन् नगरे अस्ति? (In which city is the Satyagraha Ashram?)
questions.answer: अहमदाबादनगरे
questions.explanation: The ashram stands near Ahmedabad in Gujarat, on the bank of the Sabarmati river.

questions.question: आश्रमः कस्याः नद्याः तीरे विद्यते? (On the bank of which river does the ashram stand?)

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमं कः स्थापितवान्? (Who established the Satyagraha Ashram?)
questions.answer: महात्मा गान्धी
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi founded the ashram in 1915 after his return from South Africa.

questions.question: 'सत्याग्रहः' इति पदं केन प्रकारेण निष्पन्नम्? (How is the word सत्याग्रहः formed?)
questions.answer: सत्य + आग्रहः
questions.explanation: सत्य (truth) + आग्रह (firm insistence) = सत्याग्रह, joined by दीर्घसन्धि (अ + आ = आ).

questions.question: 'सत्याग्रह' शब्दस्य समुचितः अर्थः कः? (What is the correct meaning of 'satyagraha'?)

questions.answer: सत्यस्य दृढः आग्रहः (firm insistence on truth)
questions.explanation: Satyagraha is holding firmly to truth — resisting injustice by truth-force, not violence.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमस्य अपरं नाम किम्? (What is the other name of the Satyagraha Ashram?)
questions.answer: साबरमती-आश्रमः
questions.explanation: Because it stands on the Sabarmati bank, people also call it the Sabarmati Ashram.

questions.question: अहमदाबादनगरं कस्मिन् राज्ये अस्ति? (Ahmedabad is in which state?)
questions.answer: गुर्जरराज्ये (Gujarat)
questions.explanation: The lesson says: भारतस्य पश्चिमभागे गुर्जरराज्ये अहमदाबादनाम नगरम् अस्ति।

questions.question: आश्रमस्य मुख्यम् उद्देश्यं किम् आसीत्? (What was the main purpose of the ashram?)
options: सत्याहिंसयोः अभ्यासः (practice of truth and non-violence)
questions.answer: सत्याहिंसयोः अभ्यासः (practice of truth and non-violence)
questions.explanation: The ashram was the living laboratory where satyagraha — truth and non-violence — was practised daily.

questions.question: 'आश्रमः' इति पदस्य भावः कः? (What does the word आश्रम convey?)
options: सरल-अनुशासितजीवनस्य स्थानम् (a place of simple, disciplined living)
questions.answer: सरल-अनुशासितजीवनस्य स्थानम् (a place of simple, disciplined living)
questions.explanation: An ashram is a hermitage — a community devoted to disciplined, simple living and shared ideals.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः कस्मिन् वर्षे स्थापितः? (In which year was the Satyagraha Ashram founded?)
questions.explanation: Gandhiji founded it in 1915, the same year he returned to India from South Africa.

questions.question: आश्रमः प्रथमं कुत्र स्थापितः? (Where was the ashram first established?)
questions.answer: कोचरबग्रामे
questions.explanation: It was first set up at the village Kochrab near Ahmedabad in 1915, and moved to the Sabarmati bank in 1917.

questions.question: आश्रमः कस्मिन् वर्षे साबरमतीनद्याः तीरं नीतः? (In which year was the ashram shifted to the Sabarmati bank?)
questions.explanation: In 1917 the ashram moved from Kochrab to its permanent home on the bank of the Sabarmati.

questions.question: गान्धिमहोदयः १९१५ तमे वर्षे कस्मात् देशात् भारतं प्रत्यागतः? (From which country did Gandhiji return to India in 1915?)
questions.answer: दक्षिण-आफ्रिकादेशात्
questions.explanation: Gandhiji returned from South Africa in January 1915, where he had first developed satyagraha.

questions.question: गान्धिमहोदयस्य कुटीरस्य नाम किम्? (What is the name of Gandhiji's cottage in the ashram?)
questions.answer: हृदयकुञ्जः
questions.explanation: Gandhiji's simple cottage at the Sabarmati Ashram is famous as हृदयकुञ्ज (Hriday Kunj).

questions.question: दाण्डीयात्रा कस्मिन् वर्षे अभवत्? (In which year did the Dandi March take place?)
questions.explanation: The Dandi Salt March began from the Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930.

questions.question: दाण्डीयात्रा कस्य विरोधे आसीत्? (The Dandi March was a protest against what?)
questions.answer: लवणकरस्य (the salt tax)
questions.explanation: The 1930 Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March) protested the British salt tax and salt monopoly.

questions.question: दाण्डीयात्रायाः आरम्भः कदा अभवत्? (On what date did the Dandi March begin?)
questions.explanation: Gandhiji and his companions set out from the ashram for Dandi on 12 March 1930.

questions.question: दाण्डीयात्रां प्रारभ्य गान्धिमहोदयः किं प्रतिज्ञातवान्? (Starting on the Dandi March, what did Gandhiji vow?)

questions.answer: स्वतन्त्रतां विना आश्रमं न प्रतिगमिष्यामि इति (not to return to the ashram until India was free)
questions.explanation: Gandhiji vowed not to return to the Sabarmati Ashram until India attained independence.

questions.question: अधुना साबरमती-आश्रमः किंरूपेण विद्यते? (In what form does the Sabarmati Ashram exist today?)

questions.answer: राष्ट्रियस्मारकरूपेण सङ्ग्रहालयरूपेण च (as a national memorial and museum)

questions.question: गान्धिमहोदयः आफ्रिकादेशे किं विकसितवान्? (What had Gandhiji first developed in South Africa?)
questions.answer: सत्याग्रहस्य पद्धतिम् (the method of satyagraha)
questions.explanation: Gandhiji first practised satyagraha in South Africa; on returning in 1915 he founded the ashram to continue it in India.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनः कदा उत्तिष्ठन्ति स्म? (When did the ashram residents get up?)
questions.answer: ब्राह्ममुहूर्ते

questions.explanation: All gathered for collective prayer twice a day — morning and evening.

questions.answer: सूत्रं कर्तयन्ति स्म (spun thread)
questions.explanation: The charkha (spinning wheel) was used daily to spin thread for khadi cloth.

questions.answer: खादीवस्त्राणि
questions.explanation: All wore khadi — hand-spun, hand-woven cloth, the fabric of self-reliance.

questions.answer: चौर्यस्य त्यागः (non-stealing)

options: आवश्यकतायाः अधिकं न सङ्ग्रहणीयम् (not hoarding more than one needs)
questions.answer: आवश्यकतायाः अधिकं न सङ्ग्रहणीयम् (not hoarding more than one needs)
questions.explanation: अपरिग्रह = non-possession — keeping only what one genuinely needs.

questions.question: 'शरीरश्रमः' इति व्रतस्य कः अर्थः? (What does the vow शरीरश्रम mean?)
options: स्वश्रमेण एव जीविका (earning one's bread by one's own physical labour)
अन्यैः कार्यं कारयितुम् (getting work done by others)
questions.answer: स्वश्रमेण एव जीविका (earning one's bread by one's own physical labour)
questions.explanation: शरीरश्रम is 'bread-labour' — everyone must do physical work for his own bread.

questions.question: 'अस्वादः' इति व्रतस्य कः अर्थः? (What does the vow अस्वाद mean?)
questions.answer: जिह्वायाः संयमः (control of the palate)
questions.explanation: अस्वाद = control of the palate — eating simple food without greed for taste.

questions.question: 'अभयम्' इति व्रतस्य कः अर्थः? (What does the vow अभय mean?)
questions.answer: निर्भयता (fearlessness)
questions.explanation: अभय = fearlessness — freedom from fear, essential for a satyagrahi.

questions.question: 'सर्वधर्मसमभावः' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does सर्वधर्मसमभाव mean?)
options: सर्वेषु धर्मेषु समादरः (equal respect for all religions)
एकस्य एव धर्मस्य आदरः (respect for one religion only)
questions.answer: सर्वेषु धर्मेषु समादरः (equal respect for all religions)
questions.explanation: सर्वधर्मसमभाव = regarding every faith with the same goodwill and respect.

questions.question: 'स्वदेशी' इति व्रतस्य कः अर्थः? (What does the vow स्वदेशी mean?)
options: स्वदेशनिर्मितवस्तूनाम् उपयोगः (use of home-made, local goods)
questions.answer: स्वदेशनिर्मितवस्तूनाम् उपयोगः (use of home-made, local goods)
questions.explanation: स्वदेशी = preferring goods made in one's own land and serving one's neighbourhood.

questions.question: 'अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम्' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does अस्पृश्यतानिवारण mean?)
questions.answer: अस्पृश्यतायाः उन्मूलनम् (removal of untouchability)
questions.explanation: This vow means treating every human being as equal and rooting out untouchability.

questions.question: 'व्रतम्' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What is the meaning of the word व्रतम्?)
options: दृढः सङ्कल्पः / नियमः (a vow, a firm observance)
questions.answer: दृढः सङ्कल्पः / नियमः (a vow, a firm observance)
questions.explanation: A व्रत is a firm resolve or rule of conduct voluntarily observed.

questions.question: एकादशव्रतेषु प्रथमे द्वे व्रते के? (Which are the first two of the eleven vows?)
questions.answer: सत्यम् अहिंसा च
questions.explanation: Truth and non-violence head the list of the eleven ashram observances.

questions.question: 'सत्यमेव जयते' इति वाक्यं कस्मात् ग्रन्थात् गृहीतम्? (From which text is 'Satyameva Jayate' taken?)
questions.answer: मुण्डकोपनिषदः
questions.explanation: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम् occurs in the Mundaka Upanishad (3.1.6).

questions.question: 'सत्यमेव जयते' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does 'Satyameva Jayate' mean?)
options: सत्यम् एव विजयं प्राप्नोति (truth alone triumphs)
questions.answer: सत्यम् एव विजयं प्राप्नोति (truth alone triumphs)
questions.explanation: Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood — सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम्।

questions.question: भारतस्य राष्ट्रियं वाक्यं (national motto) किम्?
questions.answer: सत्यमेव जयते
questions.explanation: सत्यमेव जयते, from the Mundaka Upanishad, is inscribed below India's national emblem.

questions.question: मन्त्रे 'नानृतम्' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (In the mantra, what does नानृतम् mean?)
options: न असत्यम् (not falsehood — falsehood does not win)
questions.answer: न असत्यम् (not falsehood — falsehood does not win)
questions.explanation: नानृतम् = न + अनृतम् — 'not falsehood'; अनृत means untruth.

questions.question: 'अहिंसा परमो धर्मः' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does 'Ahimsa paramo dharmah' mean?)
options: अहिंसा एव उत्तमः धर्मः (non-violence is the highest dharma)
धर्मः परमः शत्रुः (dharma is the greatest enemy)
questions.answer: अहिंसा एव उत्तमः धर्मः (non-violence is the highest dharma)
questions.explanation: The ancient maxim, famous from the Mahabharata, declares non-violence the highest duty/virtue.

questions.question: अहिंसा केषु त्रिषु पालनीया? (In which three ways must ahimsa be observed?)
options: मनसा वाचा कर्मणा (in mind, speech and action)
धनेन बलेन यशसा (by wealth, strength and fame)
प्रातः मध्याह्ने सायम् (morning, noon and evening)
गृहे विद्यालये मार्गे (at home, school and road)
questions.answer: मनसा वाचा कर्मणा (in mind, speech and action)
questions.explanation: True ahimsa gives up injury in thought, word and deed — मनसा वाचा कर्मणा.

questions.question: 'अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायां तत्सन्निधौ वैरत्यागः' इति सूत्रं कस्य ग्रन्थस्य? (This sutra on ahimsa is from which text?)
questions.answer: पातञ्जलयोगसूत्रस्य
questions.explanation: Yoga-sutra 2.35: when one is established in non-violence, hostility ceases in his presence.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहः कस्य बलस्य उपरि आधारितः? (On what force does satyagraha rest?)
questions.answer: आत्मबलस्य / सत्यबलस्य (soul-force, truth-force)
questions.explanation: A satyagrahi resists injustice by soul-force — truth and non-violence — never by physical force.

questions.question: गान्धिमहोदयस्य मते सत्यम् अहिंसा च परस्परं कीदृशौ? (In Gandhiji's view, how are truth and non-violence related?)
options: अविभाज्यौ — सत्यं लक्ष्यम्, अहिंसा मार्गः (inseparable — truth the goal, non-violence the path)
questions.answer: अविभाज्यौ — सत्यं लक्ष्यम्, अहिंसा मार्गः (inseparable — truth the goal, non-violence the path)
questions.explanation: For Gandhiji the two were two sides of one coin: truth is the destination, ahimsa the way to it.

questions.question: 'स्वावलम्बनम्' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does स्वावलम्बनम् mean?)
options: स्वस्य कार्यं स्वयम् एव करणम् (doing one's own work oneself)
questions.answer: स्वस्य कार्यं स्वयम् एव करणम् (doing one's own work oneself)
questions.explanation: स्व + अवलम्बन = leaning on oneself; self-reliance is doing one's own work oneself.

questions.question: आश्रमे स्वावलम्बनस्य उत्तमम् उदाहरणं किम्? (What was a fine example of self-reliance in the ashram?)
options: स्वहस्तेन सूत्रं कर्तयित्वा खादीनिर्माणम् (spinning one's own thread and making khadi)
सेवकैः कार्यकरणम् (getting work done by servants)
questions.answer: स्वहस्तेन सूत्रं कर्तयित्वा खादीनिर्माणम् (spinning one's own thread and making khadi)
questions.explanation: Residents spun thread on the charkha and wore the khadi they themselves made.

questions.question: सूत्रकर्तनस्य यन्त्रं किम् उच्यते? (What is the spinning device called?)
questions.answer: चरखा (charkha)
questions.explanation: The charkha (spinning wheel) became the very symbol of self-reliance and swadeshi.

questions.question: 'खादी' इति किम्? (What is khadi?)
questions.answer: हस्तकर्तितं हस्तनिर्मितं वस्त्रम् (hand-spun, hand-woven cloth)
questions.explanation: Khadi is cloth spun and woven by hand — the fabric of svavalambana.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनः स्वकार्यं स्वयं किमर्थम् अकुर्वन्? (Why did the residents do their own work themselves?)
options: श्रमगौरवाय स्वावलम्बनाय च (for dignity of labour and self-reliance)
questions.answer: श्रमगौरवाय स्वावलम्बनाय च (for dignity of labour and self-reliance)
questions.explanation: Doing one's own work taught dignity of labour — labour itself was worship in the ashram.

questions.question: आश्रमजीवनस्य आदर्शवाक्यं किम्? (Which saying captures the ashram's way of life?)
options: सरलं जीवनम् उच्चं चिन्तनम् (simple living, high thinking)
questions.answer: सरलं जीवनम् उच्चं चिन्तनम् (simple living, high thinking)
questions.explanation: The residents lived simply — simple food, plain khadi, few possessions — while thinking high thoughts.

questions.question: छात्रः स्वावलम्बनं कथं आचरेत्? (How should a student practise self-reliance?)
options: स्वकक्षं स्वपुस्तकानि च स्वयं व्यवस्थापयेत् (keep his own room and books in order himself)
सर्वं कार्यं मातरं कारयेत् (make his mother do everything)
गृहकार्यं मित्रेण लेखयेत् (get homework written by a friend)
questions.answer: स्वकक्षं स्वपुस्तकानि च स्वयं व्यवस्थापयेत् (keep his own room and books in order himself)
questions.explanation: Self-reliance for a student begins with doing one's own daily tasks without depending on others.

questions.question: स्वदेशीव्रतम् अद्य कथम् आचरितुं शक्यते? (How can the vow of swadeshi be practised today?)
options: स्थानीयहस्तनिर्मितवस्तूनां क्रयेण (by buying local, hand-made goods)
केवलं विदेशीयवस्तुक्रयेण (by buying only foreign goods)
किमपि न क्रीत्वा (by buying nothing at all)
questions.answer: स्थानीयहस्तनिर्मितवस्तूनां क्रयेण (by buying local, hand-made goods)
questions.explanation: Swadeshi today means preferring local and hand-made products, supporting one's own neighbourhood.

questions.question: आश्रमे 'श्रमः एव पूजा' इति भावस्य कः अभिप्रायः? (What is meant by 'labour itself was worship' in the ashram?)
options: प्रत्येकं कार्यं भक्तिभावेन गौरवेण च करणीयम् (every task is to be done with devotion and dignity)
पूजायाः स्थाने श्रमः निषिद्धः (labour was forbidden during worship)
श्रमः दण्डरूपः आसीत् (labour was a punishment)
questions.answer: प्रत्येकं कार्यं भक्तिभावेन गौरवेण च करणीयम् (every task is to be done with devotion and dignity)
questions.explanation: In the ashram no work was low: sweeping, spinning and farming were all done as acts of worship.

questions.question: 'सत्याग्रहः' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः? (What is the sandhi split of सत्याग्रहः?)
questions.answer: सत्य + आग्रहः
questions.explanation: सत्य + आग्रहः = सत्याग्रहः, by दीर्घसन्धि (अ + आ = आ).

questions.question: 'सत्याग्रहः' इति पदे कः सन्धिः? (Which sandhi occurs in सत्याग्रहः?)
questions.answer: दीर्घसन्धिः
questions.explanation: अ + आ merge into the long vowel आ — this is दीर्घसन्धि.

questions.question: 'नानृतम्' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः? (What is the sandhi split of नानृतम्?)
questions.answer: न + अनृतम्
questions.explanation: न + अनृतम् = नानृतम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धि) — 'not falsehood'.

questions.question: 'सत्यमेव' इति पदस्य विच्छेदः कः? (What is the split of सत्यमेव?)
questions.answer: सत्यम् + एव
questions.explanation: सत्यम् + एव = सत्यमेव — the final म् joins the following vowel ए.

questions.question: 'परमो धर्मः' (परमः + धर्मः) इत्यत्र कः सन्धिः? (Which sandhi occurs in परमो धर्मः?)
questions.answer: विसर्गसन्धिः
questions.explanation: The visarga of परमः becomes ओ before the soft consonant ध् — विसर्गसन्धि.

questions.question: 'आश्रमे' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (Which case is in the word आश्रमे?)
questions.answer: सप्तमी
questions.explanation: आश्रमे = 'in the ashram' — सप्तमी (locative) shows place.

questions.question: 'चरखायन्त्रेण' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (Which case is in चरखायन्त्रेण?)
questions.answer: तृतीया
questions.explanation: चरखायन्त्रेण = 'by/with the charkha' — तृतीया (instrumental) shows the means.

questions.question: 'वसति' इत्यस्य बहुवचने किं रूपम्? (What is the plural of वसति?)
questions.answer: वसन्ति
questions.explanation: वस् धातु, लट्लकार: सः वसति (he dwells) → ते वसन्ति (they dwell).

questions.question: 'आश्रम' शब्दस्य प्रथमाविभक्तेः बहुवचने किं रूपम्? (What is the nominative plural of आश्रम?)
questions.answer: आश्रमाः
questions.explanation: आश्रमः (one), आश्रमौ (two), आश्रमाः (many) — a-stem masculine, प्रथमा.

questions.question: 'आश्रमे सर्वे जनाः स्वकार्यं स्वयम् एव कुर्वन्ति।' — वाक्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does this sentence mean?)
options: In the ashram all people do their own work themselves.
In the ashram nobody does any work.
In the ashram servants do all the work.
In the ashram only Gandhiji works.
questions.answer: In the ashram all people do their own work themselves.
questions.explanation: सर्वे जनाः = all people; स्वकार्यम् = own work; स्वयम् एव कुर्वन्ति = do (it) themselves.

questions.question: 'आश्रमवासिनः प्रातः सायं च प्रार्थनां कुर्वन्ति स्म।' — कः अर्थः? (What does this sentence mean?)
options: The ashram residents used to pray in the morning and evening.
The residents used to sleep morning and evening.
The residents prayed only once a year.
The residents used to sing at noon.
questions.answer: The ashram residents used to pray in the morning and evening.
questions.explanation: प्रातः सायं च = morning and evening; कुर्वन्ति स्म = used to do.

questions.question: 'आश्रमे कोऽपि सेवकः नासीत्।' — कः अर्थः? (What does this sentence mean?)
options: There was no servant at all in the ashram.
There was one servant in the ashram.
Everyone in the ashram was a servant.
The servant was absent that day.
questions.answer: There was no servant at all in the ashram.
questions.explanation: कोऽपि (कः + अपि) = anyone at all; नासीत् (न + आसीत्) = was not.

questions.question: 'मिलित्वा' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (What does मिलित्वा mean?)
questions.answer: having gathered together
questions.explanation: मिलित्वा is the gerund of मिल् — 'having met/gathered'; सर्वे मिलित्वा प्रार्थनां कुर्वन्ति स्म।

questions.question: 'The ashram is on the bank of the river.' — संस्कृतेन किं वाक्यम्? (Which is the correct Sanskrit?)
questions.answer: आश्रमः नद्याः तीरे अस्ति।
questions.explanation: आश्रमः (प्रथमा subject) + नद्याः (षष्ठी 'of the river') + तीरे (सप्तमी 'on the bank') + अस्ति.

questions.question: 'Truth alone triumphs.' — संस्कृतेन किम्? (What is the Sanskrit for this?)
questions.answer: सत्यमेव जयते।
questions.explanation: सत्यम् + एव (alone) + जयते (triumphs) — the Mundaka Upanishad mantra.

questions.question: 'आश्रमे भोजनं सरलम् आसीत्।' — कः अर्थः? (What does this sentence mean?)
options: In the ashram the food was simple.
In the ashram the food was costly.
The food in the ashram was foreign.
questions.answer: In the ashram the food was simple.
questions.explanation: भोजनम् = food; सरलम् = simple; आसीत् = was (लङ्लकार of अस्).

questions.question: 'गान्धिमहोदयस्य कुटीरं हृदयकुञ्जः इति नाम्ना प्रसिद्धम्।' — कः अर्थः? (What does this sentence mean?)
options: Gandhiji's cottage is famous by the name Hriday Kunj.
Gandhiji built a garden called Hriday Kunj.
Hriday Kunj is the name of the river.
questions.answer: Gandhiji's cottage is famous by the name Hriday Kunj.
questions.explanation: कुटीरम् = cottage; नाम्ना = by the name; प्रसिद्धम् = famous.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः गङ्गानद्याः तीरे अस्ति। (The Satyagraha Ashram is on the bank of the Ganga.)
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: It is on the bank of the Sabarmati river near Ahmedabad, not the Ganga.

questions.question: महात्मा गान्धी सत्याग्रहाश्रमं १९१५ तमे ख्रिस्ताब्दे स्थापितवान्। (Mahatma Gandhi founded the Satyagraha Ashram in 1915.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: He founded it in 1915 at Kochrab near Ahmedabad, after returning from South Africa.

questions.question: दाण्डीयात्रा १९३० तमे वर्षे साबरमती-आश्रमात् प्रारब्धा। (The Dandi March began from the Sabarmati Ashram in 1930.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: Gandhiji set out from the ashram on the Salt March on 12 March 1930.

questions.question: आश्रमे बहवः सेवकाः कार्यं कुर्वन्ति स्म। (In the ashram many servants used to do the work.)
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: There was no servant at all — the residents did every task themselves.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनः एकादश व्रतानि पालयन्ति स्म। (The ashram residents observed eleven vows.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The एकादश व्रतानि were headed by सत्य and अहिंसा.

questions.question: 'सत्यमेव जयते' इति मन्त्रः मुण्डकोपनिषदः गृहीतः। (The mantra 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: It occurs in Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.6 and is India's national motto.

questions.question: अहिंसा इत्यस्य अर्थः शत्रूणां हिंसनम् इति। (Ahimsa means harming one's enemies.)
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: Ahimsa is the opposite — giving up injury to every living being in mind, speech and action.

questions.question: स्वहस्तेन सूत्रकर्तनं खादीधारणं च स्वावलम्बनस्य उदाहरणे स्तः। (Spinning one's own thread and wearing khadi are examples of self-reliance.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: Making and wearing one's own cloth is svavalambana — self-reliance — in action.

questions.question: 'सत्याग्रहः' इति पदे दीर्घसन्धिः अस्ति। (The word सत्याग्रहः contains दीर्घसन्धि.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: सत्य + आग्रहः: the vowels अ + आ merge into long आ — दीर्घसन्धि.

questions.question: 'आश्रमः अहमदाबादनगरस्य समीपे अस्ति।' इति वाक्यस्य अर्थः — 'The ashram is near the city of Ahmedabad.'
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: समीपे = near; the sentence says the ashram is near Ahmedabad city.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः ______ नद्याः तीरे विद्यते। (The Satyagraha Ashram stands on the bank of the ______ river.)
questions.answer: साबरमती
questions.explanation: The ashram stands on the bank of the Sabarmati — hence the name Sabarmati Ashram.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः ______ नगरस्य समीपे अस्ति। (The Satyagraha Ashram is near the city of ______.)
questions.answer: अहमदाबाद
questions.explanation: The ashram is near Ahmedabad in the state of Gujarat.

questions.question: आश्रमः ______ तमे ख्रिस्ताब्दे स्थापितः। (The ashram was founded in the year ______ CE.)
questions.explanation: Gandhiji established the ashram in 1915 (accept '1915').

questions.question: गान्धिमहोदयस्य कुटीरस्य नाम ______ इति। (The name of Gandhiji's cottage is ______.)
questions.answer: हृदयकुञ्जः
questions.explanation: His simple cottage at the ashram is famous as हृदयकुञ्ज (Hriday Kunj).

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनः प्रातः सायं च ______ कुर्वन्ति स्म। (The residents used to do ______ in the morning and evening.)
questions.answer: प्रार्थनाम्
questions.explanation: They gathered for collective prayer (प्रार्थना) twice a day; accept प्रार्थना/प्रार्थनाम्.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनः चरखायन्त्रेण ______ कर्तयन्ति स्म। (With the charkha the residents used to spin ______.)
questions.answer: सूत्रम्
questions.explanation: They spun thread (सूत्रम्) on the spinning wheel for khadi cloth.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनः ______ व्रतानि पालयन्ति स्म। (The residents observed ______ vows.)
questions.answer: एकादश
questions.explanation: They kept eleven (एकादश) vows headed by truth and non-violence.

questions.question: चौर्यस्य त्यागः इति व्रतं ______ इति कथ्यते। (The vow of giving up stealing is called ______.)
questions.answer: अस्तेयम्
questions.explanation: अस्तेय (non-stealing) is one of the eleven ashram vows.

questions.question: सत्यमेव ______ नानृतम्। (Complete the mantra.)
questions.answer: जयते
questions.explanation: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम् — truth alone triumphs, not falsehood (Mundaka Upanishad).

questions.question: अहिंसा परमो ______। (Complete the maxim.)
questions.answer: धर्मः
questions.explanation: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः — non-violence is the highest dharma.

questions.question: स्वस्य कार्यं स्वयम् एव करणम् ______ इति कथ्यते। (Doing one's own work oneself is called ______.)
questions.answer: स्वावलम्बनम्
questions.explanation: स्वावलम्बन = self-reliance, the great teaching of the ashram.

questions.question: हस्तकर्तितं हस्तनिर्मितं वस्त्रं ______ इति कथ्यते। (Hand-spun, hand-woven cloth is called ______.)
questions.answer: खादी
questions.explanation: Khadi is the hand-made cloth spun on the charkha — the fabric of self-reliance.

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत — न + अनृतम् = ______। (Join the sandhi.)
questions.answer: नानृतम्
questions.explanation: न + अनृतम् = नानृतम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धि).

questions.question: 'आश्रमे' इति पदे ______ विभक्तिः अस्ति। (The word आश्रमे is in the ______ case.)
questions.answer: सप्तमी
questions.explanation: आश्रमे = 'in the ashram' — locative, the seventh (सप्तमी) vibhakti.

questions.question: 'सर्वे जनाः स्वकार्यं स्वयं ______।' (कृ-धातोः लट्लकारे बहुवचनरूपं लिखत। Supply the plural present form of कृ.)
questions.answer: कुर्वन्ति
questions.explanation: कृ धातु, लट्लकार, प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचन: कुर्वन्ति — 'all people do their own work themselves'.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमः कः? सः कुत्र अस्ति? (What is the Satyagraha Ashram, and where is it?)
questions.answer: The Satyagraha Ashram is the ashram founded by Mahatma Gandhi as the home and training ground of satyagraha — the practice of truth and non-violence. It stands on the bank of the Sabarmati river near Ahmedabad in Gujarat, and is therefore also called the Sabarmati Ashram.
questions.explanation: Two points: what it is (Gandhiji's ashram for practising satyagraha) and where (Sabarmati bank, Ahmedabad, Gujarat).

questions.question: 'सत्याग्रह' इति पदस्य निर्माणम् अर्थं च लिखत। (Write the formation and meaning of the word सत्याग्रह.)
questions.answer: सत्याग्रह = सत्य (truth) + आग्रह (firm insistence), joined by दीर्घसन्धि (अ + आ = आ). It means 'firm insistence on truth' — resisting injustice by holding to truth with non-violence, relying on soul-force rather than physical force.
questions.explanation: Formation (सत्य + आग्रह, दीर्घसन्धि) and meaning (firm insistence on truth) both required.

questions.question: आश्रमः 'सत्याग्रहाश्रमः' इति नाम्ना किमर्थं प्रसिद्धः? (Why is the ashram famous by the name 'Satyagraha Ashram'?)
questions.answer: Because it was founded as the living laboratory of satyagraha: here Gandhiji and his companions practised truth and non-violence daily and trained themselves for the satyagraha struggles. Since the ideal of the ashram was सत्याग्रह — firm insistence on truth — the ashram itself took that name.
questions.explanation: The name reflects its purpose: a place for practising and training in satyagraha.

questions.question: आश्रमः कदा कुत्र च स्थापितः? कदा च साबरमतीतीरं नीतः? (When and where was the ashram founded, and when was it shifted to the Sabarmati bank?)
questions.answer: Mahatma Gandhi founded the ashram in 1915 CE at the village Kochrab near Ahmedabad, soon after returning to India from South Africa. In 1917 it was shifted to its permanent home on the bank of the Sabarmati river.
questions.explanation: Three facts: 1915, Kochrab (near Ahmedabad), shifted to Sabarmati bank in 1917.

questions.question: हृदयकुञ्जः इति किम्? (What is Hriday Kunj?)
questions.answer: हृदयकुञ्ज ('bower of the heart') is the name of Mahatma Gandhi's small, simple cottage at the Sabarmati Ashram. He lived there with Kasturba, and today it is the most visited spot of the ashram memorial.
questions.explanation: Gandhiji's cottage at the ashram, preserved today in the national memorial.

questions.question: १२ मार्च १९३० दिनाङ्के आश्रमे किं महत् कार्यम् अभवत्? (What great event took place at the ashram on 12 March 1930?)
questions.answer: On 12 March 1930 Gandhiji, with his companions, set out from the Sabarmati Ashram on the famous Dandi March — the Salt Satyagraha against the British salt tax. He vowed not to return to the ashram until India won her freedom.
questions.explanation: The Dandi (Salt) March began from the ashram on that date, with Gandhiji's vow not to return before independence.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनां प्रातःकालीनं जीवनं वर्णयत। (Describe the morning life of the ashram residents.)
questions.answer: The residents rose in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त, the early hour before dawn. Then all gathered together for the morning prayer. After the prayer each person turned to his or her allotted work — farming, spinning on the charkha, cow-service, washing and cleaning.
questions.explanation: Early rising, collective prayer, then allotted work — the disciplined start of the ashram day.

questions.question: आश्रमे सेवकाः किमर्थं न आसन्? (Why were there no servants in the ashram?)
questions.answer: Because self-reliance (स्वावलम्बन) and bread-labour (शरीरश्रम) were core ashram values: every resident had to do his own work himself — washing his own clothes, cleaning his own utensils, growing food. Keeping servants would have gone against the dignity of labour that the ashram taught.
questions.explanation: No servants because self-help and dignity of labour were vows of the community.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनः कानि कानि कार्याणि कुर्वन्ति स्म? त्रीणि लिखत। (Write any three kinds of work the residents used to do.)
questions.answer: Any three: farming in the fields (कृषिकार्यम्), spinning thread on the charkha (सूत्रकर्तनम्), cow-service (गोसेवा), washing their own clothes, cleaning their own utensils, and keeping the ashram clean.
questions.explanation: Any three of: farming, spinning, cow-care, washing clothes, cleaning utensils, cleanliness work.

questions.question: एकादशव्रतेषु कानिचन चत्वारि व्रतानि सार्थं लिखत। (Write any four of the eleven vows with their meanings.)
questions.answer: Any four, e.g.: सत्यम् — truth in thought, word and deed; अहिंसा — non-violence towards every creature; अस्तेयम् — non-stealing; अपरिग्रहः — non-possession, keeping only what one needs. (Also: ब्रह्मचर्यम्, शरीरश्रमः, अस्वादः, अभयम्, सर्वधर्मसमभावः, स्वदेशी, अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम्.)
questions.explanation: Any four vows correctly named with meanings earn full marks.

questions.question: 'अपरिग्रहः' 'अस्वादः' च — एतयोः व्रतयोः अर्थं लिखत। (Write the meaning of the vows अपरिग्रह and अस्वाद.)
questions.answer: अपरिग्रहः (non-possession) means not accumulating or hoarding more than one genuinely needs — living with few possessions. अस्वादः (control of the palate) means eating simple, wholesome food for nourishment, without greed for taste or delicacies.
questions.explanation: Both meanings needed: non-hoarding, and control of taste.

questions.question: 'सर्वधर्मसमभावः' 'अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम्' च — एतयोः व्रतयोः अर्थं महत्त्वं च लिखत। (Explain the meaning and importance of the vows सर्वधर्मसमभाव and अस्पृश्यतानिवारण.)
questions.answer: सर्वधर्मसमभावः means equal respect for all religions — regarding every faith with the same goodwill; it builds harmony in a land of many religions. अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम् means the removal of untouchability — treating every human being as equal; Gandhiji held this social reform essential for a just and united society.
questions.explanation: Meanings plus their social importance: religious harmony and human equality.

questions.question: 'सत्यमेव जयते...' इति मन्त्रं पूर्णं लिखित्वा तस्य अर्थं लिखत। (Write the full mantra 'Satyameva Jayate...' and give its meaning.)
questions.answer: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः। Meaning: Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood; by truth is laid out the divine path (the path leading to the gods). It is from the Mundaka Upanishad and is India's national motto.
questions.explanation: Mantra line plus meaning; source Mundaka Upanishad, national motto.

questions.question: 'अहिंसा परमो धर्मः' — अस्य वाक्यस्य भावं स्पष्टीकुरुत। (Explain the idea of 'Ahimsa paramo dharmah'.)
questions.answer: The maxim declares non-violence to be the highest dharma — the supreme duty and virtue. True ahimsa is not mere avoidance of physical harm: it gives up injury to every living being in mind, speech and action (मनसा वाचा कर्मणा), and includes love and compassion even towards opponents, as Gandhiji showed in satyagraha.
questions.explanation: Highest dharma; threefold observance (thought, word, deed); positive sense of love/compassion.

questions.question: योगसूत्रस्य 'अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायां तत्सन्निधौ वैरत्यागः' इति सूत्रस्य अर्थं लिखत। (Give the meaning of the Yoga-sutra on ahimsa.)
questions.answer: When a person is firmly established in non-violence (अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायाम्), then in his presence (तत्सन्निधौ) beings give up their hostility (वैरत्यागः). That is, perfected ahimsa radiates peace — even natural enemies cease to quarrel near such a person, as was often seen around Gandhiji.
questions.explanation: Word meanings: established in ahimsa, in his presence, abandonment of enmity.

questions.question: स्वावलम्बनं किम्? आश्रमे तस्य एकम् उदाहरणं लिखत। (What is self-reliance? Give one example of it from the ashram.)
questions.answer: स्वावलम्बनम् (self-reliance) is doing one's own work oneself instead of depending on others. Example from the ashram: the residents spun their own thread on the charkha and made their own khadi cloth; they also washed their own clothes and cleaned their own utensils, keeping no servants.
questions.explanation: Definition plus any one ashram example (spinning/khadi, washing, cleaning, no servants).

questions.question: खादी किमर्थं महत्त्वपूर्णा आसीत्? (Why was khadi important?)
questions.answer: Khadi — hand-spun, hand-woven cloth — was the living symbol of self-reliance and swadeshi. Spinning one's own cloth freed people from dependence on foreign mill cloth, gave work and income to villagers, taught dignity of labour, and united the nation in a daily act of quiet self-rule.
questions.explanation: Khadi = symbol of svavalamban and swadeshi; economic self-help and dignity of labour.

questions.question: छात्रः सरलजीवनं कथम् आचरेत्? द्वे उदाहरणे लिखत। (How should a student practise simple living? Give two examples.)
questions.answer: Any two: eating simple, wholesome food without fuss; wearing plain, clean clothes without show; avoiding waste of money, food, water and electricity; keeping few but useful possessions (अपरिग्रह); doing one's own daily tasks; spending more time on study and service than on luxuries.
questions.explanation: Any two concrete habits of simplicity and self-help earn full marks.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत — (a) सत्याग्रहः (b) नानृतम् (c) कोऽपि। (Split the sandhi in these three words.)
questions.answer: (a) सत्याग्रहः = सत्य + आग्रहः (दीर्घसन्धिः, अ + आ = आ). (b) नानृतम् = न + अनृतम् (दीर्घसन्धिः, अ + अ = आ). (c) कोऽपि = कः + अपि (विसर्गसन्धिः — कः + अपि → कोऽपि with अवग्रह).
questions.explanation: Two दीर्घ splits and one विसर्ग split, all from the lesson.

questions.question: अधोलिखितपदानां विभक्तिं तत्कार्यं च लिखत — आश्रमे, नद्याः, चरखायन्त्रेण। (State the case and its role for: आश्रमे, नद्याः, चरखायन्त्रेण.)
questions.answer: आश्रमे = सप्तमी (locative) — 'in the ashram', shows place. नद्याः = षष्ठी (genitive) — 'of the river', shows relation/possession (साबरमतीनद्याः तीरे). चरखायन्त्रेण = तृतीया (instrumental) — 'by/with the charkha', shows the means.
questions.explanation: सप्तमी place, षष्ठी of-relation, तृतीया means — with meanings.

questions.question: आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अनुवादं कुरुत — (a) आश्रमे जीवनं सरलं नियमबद्धं च आसीत्। (b) सर्वे खादीवस्त्राणि धारयन्ति स्म। (Translate into English.)
questions.answer: (a) In the ashram, life was simple and disciplined (bound by rules). (b) All used to wear khadi clothes.
questions.explanation: नियमबद्धम् = rule-bound/disciplined; धारयन्ति स्म = used to wear.

questions.question: संस्कृतेन अनुवादं कुरुत — (a) Gandhiji founded the ashram. (b) The residents do their own work. (Translate into Sanskrit.)
questions.answer: (a) गान्धिमहोदयः आश्रमं स्थापितवान्। (b) आश्रमवासिनः स्वकार्यं स्वयं कुर्वन्ति। (Equivalent correct forms are acceptable, e.g. गान्धी आश्रमम् अस्थापयत्।)
questions.explanation: Simple subject-object-verb sentences using chapter vocabulary; accept equivalent correct Sanskrit.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमस्य परिचयं लिखत — स्थानम्, संस्थापकः, नामकारणम्, उद्देश्यं च। (Write an introduction to the Satyagraha Ashram — its location, founder, the reason for its name, and its purpose.)
questions.answer: The Satyagraha Ashram stands on the bank of the Sabarmati river near Ahmedabad, in the state of Gujarat in western India; from the river it is also called the Sabarmati Ashram. It was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1915, soon after his return from South Africa — first at the village Kochrab, and from 1917 at the Sabarmati bank. It is named 'Satyagraha Ashram' because it was the home of सत्याग्रह (सत्य + आग्रह, 'firm insistence on truth'), the method Gandhiji had developed for resisting injustice through truth and non-violence. The ashram's purpose was to be a living laboratory of these ideals: its residents practised truth, non-violence, self-reliance and simple living daily, kept the eleven vows, spun khadi on the charkha, served the village and trained themselves as satyagrahis. Gandhiji's simple cottage there, हृदयकुञ्ज (Hriday Kunj), remains its heart, and the ashram today is a national memorial.
questions.explanation: Location (Sabarmati/Ahmedabad/Gujarat), founder and dates (Gandhi, 1915/1917), name (satya + agraha), and purpose (training ground of satyagraha values).

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमस्य इतिहासं लिखत — कोचरबग्रामतः दाण्डीयात्रापर्यन्तम्, अद्यत्वे च आश्रमस्य स्थितिम्। (Write the history of the Satyagraha Ashram — from Kochrab to the Dandi March, and its condition today.)
questions.answer: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in 1915, where he had first forged the weapon of satyagraha. In the same year he founded the Satyagraha Ashram at the village Kochrab near Ahmedabad. In 1917 the ashram moved to open ground on the bank of the Sabarmati river, where there was room for farming, cattle and craft; there Gandhiji lived in the simple cottage Hriday Kunj. For over a decade the ashram was the nerve-centre of the freedom movement and of Gandhiji's constructive work — khadi, village service and the removal of untouchability. On 12 March 1930 Gandhiji set out from the ashram with his companions on the Dandi March, the Salt Satyagraha against the British salt tax, vowing not to return until India became free. India won independence in 1947, and today the Sabarmati Ashram is preserved as a national memorial and museum, where visitors from all over the world see Hriday Kunj, the charkha and Gandhiji's way of life.
questions.explanation: Sequence: 1915 return + Kochrab founding; 1917 shift to Sabarmati; ashram as centre of constructive work; 12 March 1930 Dandi March and the vow; today a national memorial.

questions.question: आश्रमवासिनां दिनचर्याम् अनुशासनं च विस्तरेण वर्णयत। (Describe in detail the daily routine and discipline of the ashram residents.)
questions.answer: Life in the ashram was simple and bound by rule (सरलं नियमबद्धं च). The residents rose in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त, before dawn. Morning and evening, all gathered for collective prayer (प्रार्थना), which knit the community together. After prayer each turned to allotted work: some farmed the fields (कृषिकार्यम्), some spun thread on the charkha (सूत्रकर्तनम्), some served the cows (गोसेवा). Everyone washed his own clothes and cleaned his own utensils — there was no servant in the ashram, for self-help and bread-labour (शरीरश्रम) were vows. Food was sattvik and simple, taken without greed for taste (अस्वाद). All wore khadi spun by their own hands. Cleanliness (स्वच्छता) and discipline (अनुशासनम्) were visible everywhere — in the huts, the kitchen, the fields and the daily timetable. Thus the whole day, from prayer to labour, was itself an education in truth, non-violence and self-reliance.
questions.explanation: Early rising, twice-daily prayer, allotted work (farming/spinning/cow-care), no servants, simple sattvik food, khadi, cleanliness and discipline.

questions.question: आश्रमस्य एकादश व्रतानि नामनिर्देशपूर्वकं सार्थं लिखत। एतेषां व्रतानां जीवने किं महत्त्वम्? (List the eleven ashram vows with meanings. What is their importance in life?)
questions.answer: The eleven vows (एकादश व्रतानि) are: (1) सत्यम् — truth in thought, word and deed; (2) अहिंसा — non-violence to every creature; (3) ब्रह्मचर्यम् — self-control and purity; (4) अस्तेयम् — non-stealing; (5) अपरिग्रहः — non-possession, keeping only what one needs; (6) शरीरश्रमः — bread-labour, physical work for one's own bread; (7) अस्वादः — control of the palate; (8) अभयम् — fearlessness; (9) सर्वधर्मसमभावः — equal respect for all religions; (10) स्वदेशी — use of home-made, local goods; (11) अस्पृश्यतानिवारणम् — removal of untouchability. Importance: these vows turn great ideals into small daily habits. They purify personal character (truth, self-control, simplicity), build a just society (equality of religions, end of untouchability, dignity of labour) and strengthen the nation (swadeshi, fearlessness). By living them, the ashram residents became strong and pure — values were not preached but practised.
questions.explanation: All eleven vows with brief meanings, plus their personal, social and national importance.

questions.question: सत्यम् अहिंसा च गान्धिदर्शनस्य आधारौ। मुण्डकोपनिषदः मन्त्रं, 'अहिंसा परमो धर्मः' इति वाक्यं, योगसूत्रं च उद्धृत्य एतयोः मूल्ययोः विवेचनं कुरुत। (Truth and non-violence are the foundations of Gandhian philosophy. Discuss these two values, quoting the Mundaka mantra, 'Ahimsa paramo dharmah', and the Yoga-sutra.)
questions.answer: Truth (सत्यम्) was for Gandhiji the highest reality — he even said 'Truth is God'. The Mundaka Upanishad proclaims: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः — 'Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood; by truth is laid the divine path.' This mantra, now India's national motto, teaches that however strong falsehood may seem, final victory belongs to truth. Non-violence (अहिंसा) is the refusal to injure any being in mind, speech or action — मनसा वाचा कर्मणा. The ancient maxim अहिंसा परमो धर्मः declares it the highest dharma, and the Yoga-sutra adds: अहिंसाप्रतिष्ठायां तत्सन्निधौ वैरत्यागः — hostility itself ceases in the presence of one established in ahimsa. In Gandhian philosophy the two are inseparable: truth is the goal, non-violence the only path to it; means must be as pure as ends. Satyagraha, built on these values, resisted injustice with soul-force, converted opponents rather than crushing them, and showed the world — as at Sabarmati and Dandi — that truth and love are stronger than force.
questions.explanation: Quote and explain all three sayings; show truth as goal, ahimsa as path, and their union in satyagraha.

questions.question: 'सरलं जीवनम् उच्चं चिन्तनम्' — आश्रमजीवनस्य आलोकेन अस्य आदर्शस्य विवेचनं कृत्वा, अद्यत्वे छात्रजीवने तस्य प्रयोगं लिखत। (Discuss the ideal of 'simple living, high thinking' in the light of ashram life, and write how it can be applied in student life today.)
questions.answer: In the ashram, simple living was a discipline, not a deprivation. The residents lived in plain huts, ate simple sattvik food (अस्वाद), wore self-spun khadi, kept few possessions (अपरिग्रह) and did all their own work (स्वावलम्बन, शरीरश्रम) — there was not a single servant. Yet their thinking was of the highest: truth, non-violence, the freedom of India and the service of the poorest. Because their needs were small, their minds were free for great aims — labour itself became worship. A student today can live this ideal by: keeping needs and possessions few and avoiding show and waste; eating simple food and dressing plainly; doing his or her own daily work — room, clothes, books — without depending on others; limiting distractions (gadgets, fashion) and giving the saved time to study, reading and helping others; preferring local and hand-made goods (स्वदेशी); and setting the mind on high aims — knowledge, character and service — rather than on luxury. Simplicity outside creates strength and clarity within.
questions.explanation: Ashram evidence of simplicity (food, khadi, few possessions, self-work) joined to high aims; then at least four concrete student applications.

questions.question: पाठात् उदाहरणानि गृहीत्वा लिखत — (a) दीर्घसन्धेः विसर्गसन्धेः च द्वे द्वे उदाहरणे सविच्छेदम्, (b) तिसृणां विभक्तीनां पदानि सप्रयोजनम्, (c) 'आश्रम' शब्दस्य प्रथमायाः त्रीणि रूपाणि, (d) 'कुर्वन्ति स्म' 'आसीत्' इत्यनयोः अर्थः। (Taking examples from the lesson, write: (a) two examples each of dirgha- and visarga-sandhi with splits, (b) words of three different cases with their roles, (c) the three nominative forms of आश्रम, (d) the meaning of कुर्वन्ति स्म and आसीत्.)
questions.answer: (a) दीर्घसन्धिः: सत्य + आग्रहः = सत्याग्रहः (अ + आ = आ); न + अनृतम् = नानृतम् (अ + अ = आ). विसर्गसन्धिः: परमः + धर्मः = परमो धर्मः (visarga → ओ before a soft consonant); कः + अपि = कोऽपि (with अवग्रह). (b) Three cases from the text: चरखायन्त्रेण — तृतीया, 'by the charkha' (means); नद्याः — षष्ठी, 'of the river' (relation); आश्रमे — सप्तमी, 'in the ashram' (place). (Also acceptable: प्रार्थनाम् — द्वितीया object; आफ्रिकादेशात् — पञ्चमी 'from'.) (c) आश्रम, प्रथमा: एकवचनम् आश्रमः, द्विवचनम् आश्रमौ, बहुवचनम् आश्रमाः. (d) कुर्वन्ति स्म = 'they used to do' (present लट् + स्म expresses past habit); आसीत् = 'was' (लङ्लकार of अस्).
questions.explanation: Four parts: sandhi with splits, case roles, shabda-rupa of आश्रम, and the two verb forms.

questions.question: सत्याग्रहाश्रमम् अधिकृत्य पञ्च सरलानि संस्कृतवाक्यानि देवनागर्या लिखत, प्रत्येकस्य आङ्ग्लार्थं च ददत। (Write five simple Sanskrit sentences in Devanagari about the Satyagraha Ashram, giving the English meaning of each.)
questions.answer:
1. सत्याग्रहाश्रमः साबरमतीनद्याः तीरे अस्ति। (The Satyagraha Ashram is on the bank of the Sabarmati river.)
2. महात्मा गान्धी एनम् आश्रमं स्थापितवान्। (Mahatma Gandhi established this ashram.)
3. आश्रमवासिनः प्रातः सायं च प्रार्थनां कुर्वन्ति स्म। (The residents used to pray in the morning and evening.)
4. ते चरखायन्त्रेण सूत्रं कर्तयन्ति स्म। (They used to spin thread on the charkha.)
5. आश्रमे सर्वे स्वकार्यं स्वयम् एव कुर्वन्ति स्म। (In the ashram all used to do their own work themselves.)
(Any five correct simple sentences on the ashram, with English meanings, are acceptable.)
questions.explanation: Simple subject-object-verb sentences built from chapter vocabulary; accept any correct equivalents.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'भारतस्य पश्चिमभागे गुर्जरराज्ये अहमदाबादनाम नगरम् अस्ति। तस्य समीपे साबरमतीनद्याः तीरे सत्याग्रहाश्रमः विद्यते। महात्मा गान्धी एनम् आश्रमं स्थापितवान्।' — (a) अहमदाबादनगरं कस्मिन् राज्ये अस्ति? (b) आश्रमः कस्याः नद्याः तीरे विद्यते? (c) आश्रमं कः स्थापितवान्?
questions.answer: (a) अहमदाबादनगरं गुर्जरराज्ये (Gujarat) अस्ति। (b) आश्रमः साबरमतीनद्याः तीरे विद्यते। (c) आश्रमं महात्मा गान्धी स्थापितवान्।
questions.explanation: All three answers are directly stated in the passage: Gujarat, the Sabarmati, Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'महात्मा गान्धी दक्षिण-आफ्रिकादेशात् प्रत्यागत्य १९१५ तमे वर्षे कोचरबग्रामे आश्रमं स्थापितवान्। ततः १९१७ तमे वर्षे आश्रमः साबरमतीनद्याः तीरं नीतः।' — (a) गान्धी कस्मात् देशात् प्रत्यागतः? (b) आश्रमः प्रथमं कुत्र स्थापितः? (c) कदा सः साबरमतीतीरं नीतः?
questions.answer: (a) गान्धी दक्षिण-आफ्रिकादेशात् (from South Africa) प्रत्यागतः। (b) आश्रमः प्रथमं कोचरबग्रामे स्थापितः। (c) १९१७ तमे वर्षे सः साबरमतीनद्याः तीरं नीतः।
questions.explanation: South Africa; Kochrab village (1915); shifted to the Sabarmati bank in 1917.

questions.question: Read and answer: 'On 12 March 1930 Gandhiji set out from the Sabarmati Ashram with his companions on the Dandi March, vowing not to return to the ashram until India won her freedom.' — (a) What was the Dandi March against? (b) What vow did Gandhiji take on setting out? (c) What does this vow show about his commitment to satyagraha?
questions.answer: (a) The Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) was against the British salt tax and salt monopoly. (b) He vowed not to return to the Sabarmati Ashram until India attained freedom. (c) The vow shows total commitment: for a satyagrahi, a vow (व्रत) is unbreakable — Gandhiji staked his beloved home itself on the truth of his cause, showing that satyagraha demands complete self-sacrifice, not half-hearted effort.
questions.explanation: Salt tax; the vow of not returning before freedom; analysis — a satyagrahi's vow as total commitment.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'आश्रमवासिनः ब्राह्ममुहूर्ते उत्तिष्ठन्ति स्म। सर्वे मिलित्वा प्रार्थनां कुर्वन्ति स्म। केचन कृषिकार्यं कुर्वन्ति स्म, केचन सूत्रं कर्तयन्ति स्म। आश्रमे कोऽपि सेवकः नासीत्।' — (a) आश्रमवासिनः कदा उत्तिष्ठन्ति स्म? (b) प्रार्थनां कथं कुर्वन्ति स्म? (c) 'कोऽपि सेवकः नासीत्' — अनेन किं ज्ञायते?
questions.answer: (a) ते ब्राह्ममुहूर्ते (in the early hour before dawn) उत्तिष्ठन्ति स्म। (b) सर्वे मिलित्वा (all together, collectively) प्रार्थनां कुर्वन्ति स्म। (c) From 'there was no servant at all' we learn that the residents practised self-reliance (स्वावलम्बन) and bread-labour — every person did his own work himself, and no work was considered low.
questions.explanation: Early rising, collective prayer, and the inference of self-reliance from the absence of servants.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'आश्रमवासिनः एकादश व्रतानि पालयन्ति स्म — सत्यम्, अहिंसा, ब्रह्मचर्यम्, अस्तेयम्, अपरिग्रहः, शरीरश्रमः, अस्वादः, अभयम्, सर्वधर्मसमभावः, स्वदेशी, अस्पृश्यतानिवारणं च।' — (a) आश्रमवासिनः कति व्रतानि पालयन्ति स्म? (b) प्रथमे द्वे व्रते के? (c) 'शरीरश्रमः' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: (a) ते एकादश (eleven) व्रतानि पालयन्ति स्म। (b) प्रथमे द्वे व्रते सत्यम् अहिंसा च। (c) शरीरश्रमः means bread-labour — earning one's bread by one's own physical work; every resident had to labour with his own body.
questions.explanation: Eleven vows; truth and non-violence first; bread-labour explained.

questions.question: Read and answer: 'Ashram residents kept the vow of अपरिग्रह (non-possession) — no one kept more than he needed — and the vow of अस्वाद (control of the palate) — food was simple and taken without greed for taste.' — (a) What is अपरिग्रह? (b) What is अस्वाद? (c) Suggest one way a student can practise each of these two vows today.
questions.answer: (a) अपरिग्रह is non-possession — not accumulating more than one genuinely needs. (b) अस्वाद is control of the palate — eating simple, wholesome food without craving for taste. (c) A student can practise अपरिग्रह by keeping only needed books, clothes and gadgets and donating extras; and अस्वाद by choosing simple, healthy food (e.g. home food over junk food) and not demanding special dishes.
questions.explanation: Definitions of both vows plus one concrete modern application for each.

questions.question: मन्त्रं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः।' — (a) मन्त्रः कस्मात् ग्रन्थात्? (b) 'नानृतम्' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदं अर्थं च लिखत। (c) मन्त्रस्य केन्द्रीयः भावः कः?
questions.answer: (a) मन्त्रः मुण्डकोपनिषदः (from the Mundaka Upanishad; it is India's national motto). (b) नानृतम् = न + अनृतम् (दीर्घसन्धिः); अर्थः — 'not falsehood', i.e. falsehood does not triumph. (c) The central idea: victory finally belongs to truth alone, never to falsehood; the divine path is laid out by truth, so one should hold to truth in all circumstances.
questions.explanation: Source, sandhi split with meaning, and the central message of the mantra.

questions.question: Read and answer: 'The residents spun thread with their own hands and made khadi cloth. They used only swadeshi goods. Their living was simple, their thinking high. Labour itself was their worship.' — (a) What is khadi? (b) What does 'labour itself was worship' mean? (c) Give one way you can follow swadeshi in your own life.
questions.answer: (a) Khadi is hand-spun, hand-woven cloth, made by the residents themselves on the charkha. (b) 'Labour itself was worship' means every task — spinning, sweeping, farming — was done with devotion and dignity; no work was considered low, and honest work was valued as highly as prayer. (c) Example: preferring locally made or hand-made products (khadi cloth, local foods, village crafts) over imported factory goods; any one sensible example is acceptable.
questions.explanation: Khadi definition, dignity-of-labour explanation, and a personal swadeshi application.

questions.question: वाक्यं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'आश्रमवासिनः चरखायन्त्रेण सूत्रं कर्तयन्ति स्म।' — (a) 'चरखायन्त्रेण' इति पदे का विभक्तिः, किं च तस्याः प्रयोजनम्? (b) 'सूत्रम्' इति पदे का विभक्तिः? (c) 'कर्तयन्ति स्म' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: (a) चरखायन्त्रेण — तृतीया विभक्तिः (instrumental); it shows the means, 'by/with the charkha'. (b) सूत्रम् — द्वितीया विभक्तिः (accusative), the object of the verb — 'thread' is what was spun. (c) कर्तयन्ति स्म = 'they used to spin' — the present tense (लट्) with स्म expresses a past habit.
questions.explanation: तृतीया of means, द्वितीया object, and लट् + स्म = past habitual.

questions.question: गद्यांशं पठित्वा उत्तरत — 'आश्रमे जीवनं सरलं नियमबद्धं च आसीत्। भोजनं सात्त्विकं सरलं च आसीत्। सर्वे खादीवस्त्राणि धारयन्ति स्म।' — (a) आश्रमे जीवनं कीदृशम् आसीत्? (b) भोजनं कीदृशम् आसीत्? (c) तृतीयवाक्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अनुवादं कुरुत।
questions.answer: (a) आश्रमे जीवनं सरलं नियमबद्धं च आसीत् — life was simple and disciplined. (b) भोजनं सात्त्विकं सरलं च आसीत् — the food was sattvik (pure) and simple. (c) Translation of the third sentence: 'All used to wear khadi clothes.'
questions.explanation: Comprehension of two descriptive sentences and translation of the third.
